title: Artificial Intelligence 2026 - India | Global Practice Guides | Chambers and Partners
snippet: With the increasing reliance on AI technologies by the legal fraternity, several challenges, such as confidentiality breaches, fabricated legal precedents in pleadings, and algorithmic biases in generative AI tools, exist. There are already instances of lawyers relying on non-existent case law in their pleadings or filing petitions with AI-generated arguments, which highlight the need to exercise caution while using such technologies. At times, a client’s confidential information is fed into AI [...] At the same time, the increasing use of generative AI (GenAI) systems across sectors has intensified concerns relating to copyright infringement, deepfakes, data protection, misinformation, cybersecurity, algorithmic accountability, and consumer harms. Indian regulators, courts, and policy-making authorities have been addressing these concerns through a combination of existing legislation, sector-specific regulations, advisories/guidelines, and judicial intervention. [...] Product liability and safety issues would be governed under the Indian Consumer Protection Act 2019 (CPA) and general negligence principles. When AI systems malfunction, generate unsafe outputs, or operate without safeguards, developers may face exposure. The potential risks become more evident with generative and agentic systems due to the unpredictability of outputs and minimal human oversight.

title: IT Compliance Regulations 2026: New Rules You Need to Know
snippet:
Generative AI models such as LLMs, when integrated into customer support, fraud detection, or decision-making tools, create new challenges for the entire risk & compliance industry. These include content provenance, response accuracy, and potential liability for decisions made or informed by AI outputs. [...] At the same time, compliance leaders face new challenges:

   Expanding third-party oversight requirements
   Increased use of AI systems without sufficient governance
   Greater regulatory pressure to address digital assets, crypto assets, and emerging technologies
   Rising costs of non-compliance due to increasing state insurance compliance requirements through NAIC Model Act enforcement, international MiCA regulation, and the GTIA Cybersecurity Trustmark [...] Organizations that develop, deploy, or integrate AI systems must now navigate an evolving matrix of AI compliance mandates, including classification tiers, audit trails and readiness, and explainability obligations. These frameworks aim to manage the risks associated with generative AI, autonomous decision-making systems, and agentic AI models that interact with customers, systems, and data autonomously.
